questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Tanzania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Regions” part of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: Tanzania's regions are: Arusha · Dar es Salaam · Dodoma · Geita · Iringa · Kagera · Katavi · Kigoma · Kilimanjaro · Lindi · Manyara · Mara · Mbeya · Morogoro · Mtwara · Mwanza · Njombe · Pemba North · Pemba South · Pwani · Rukwa · Ruvuma · Shinyanga · Simiyu · Singida · Songwe · Tabora · Tanga · Zanzibar Central/South · Zanzibar North · Zanzibar Urban/West

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Tanzania?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: The official languages are Kiswahili and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is next to Africa's biggest lake, Lake _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Lake”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: It is next to Africa's biggest lake, Lake Victoria.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The two countries joined to form the United Republic of Tanzania in April _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: The two countries joined to form the United Republic of Tanzania in April 1964.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Mainland Tanzania (formerly Tanganyika) received independence in December _____, while Zanzibar gained her independence in January 1964, through a revolution.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: Mainland Tanzania (formerly Tanganyika) received independence in December 1961, while Zanzibar gained her independence in January 1964, through a revolution.
